doc.title: Nancy Wilson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Songs as high points of songwriting
summary: She tries to name great lyrics, recalling Over the Weekend and Lush Life songs.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: It’s interesting. You pull out a line, because at some point we’re talking about a song and a story. I’m wondering if any particular songs, other than Guess Who, or even lyrics, stick in your mind as just an amazing example of the height of songwriting.
Oh, wow. No, it wouldn’t come to mind now.
If something comes to your mind, just digress to it.
Okay. I remember there’s a song that Johnny Mathis did, and I did it. It was a great song. But I can’t remember right now. Oh well. Over the Weekend.
Oh. That is – well, all the songs on – what the one about the [?]? Is that Midnight Sun? The songs on Lush Life that have lyrics are amazing, including the one you just mentioned.
